items.title: Vehicle recognition (Autocharge)
items.notes: The charger reads the car's identifier and sends it as the ID. Never typed in: the gateway records it on a normal session and it is stored against a company vehicle only after consent. Mostly DC chargers; some car brands randomise the identifier. Needed before the company rules "vehicles only" and "vehicle and driver" can be enforced.

items.title: Whitelist: private chargers and discounts
items.notes: Built end to end on the operator side: private sites (hidden from the map except for whitelisted drivers and refused at the charger for everyone else), whitelists covering chosen sites with drivers added by email or phone number, and a discount on the energy price (100% = free energy; any session, time or idle fee in the tariff still applies). Left: see it in the driver app and check the screens in a browser.

items.title: Corporate charging: companies and their driver accounts
items.notes: Admin and database built: a company has drivers (app accounts added by email or phone number, each with optional RFID cards), vehicles (plate, model, VIN for reference) and a rule for who may charge on its bill. Still to do: the gateway enforcing the vehicle rules.

items.title: Gateway: whitelist discount and private sites at the charger
items.notes: The gateway takes a whitelist discount off the energy price at session start (best discount wins; time, parking and flat fees are not discounted) and refuses a driver who is not whitelisted at a private site. Covered by 7 integration scenarios.

items.title: Multi-country on one backend (Malaysia + Singapore)
items.notes: One CSMS and one app for every country. Done: each operator account has one country, fixed when Voltara creates it (cannot be changed); sites follow it; forms, phone codes, registration numbers (SSM/TIN/SST or UEN/GST) and the currency symbol follow it; local demo has a Singapore and a Malaysia operator. To build: one Stripe account per country, GST on Singapore invoices and InvoiceNow, LTA licensing and reporting, country shown per operator in a platform console, the driver app showing prices in the site's currency.

items.title: Sub-operators: an operator's own customers
items.notes: An operator can create sub-operator accounts for its customers (e.g. a condo or fleet managing its own chargers and whitelists). A sub-operator inherits the parent's country and cannot change it. Builds on operator accounts; whitelists and private sites are the first step.

Operator accounts: Voltara creates a customer's account and picks its country
items.notes: KIV. A screen for Voltara (platform owner) to create an operator account for a customer: company name, first login, and the country (Malaysia or Singapore), which can never be changed afterwards. The operator then logs in and manages only its own chargers. The database already holds the fixed country per operator; today accounts are still created by hand. Self sign-up by operators comes after this.
